name: Deictic here or there with Inversion
pattern: Clause[stressed locative here/there + V + full NP], or here/there + pronoun + V

entry.name: Deictic here or there with Inversion
entry.pattern: Clause[stressed locative here/there + V + full NP], or here/there + pronoun + V

1.definition: Draws attention to an arrival, presence or departure in the relevant perceptual setting.

examples.note: Constructed comparison. Ordinary order when the subject is a personal pronoun.

projection.target: A full NP typically follows come. A personal pronoun occurs before it in Here it comes. The locative can receive pointing stress, unlike the dummy subject of an existential.
projection.evidence: See the cited discussion and the constructed illustration.

curious.title: Here comes the bus
curious.summary: Starting a sentence with a stressed here or there, then the verb, points out something arriving, present or leaving.
curious.body: In Here comes the bus, here points to the place you are, the verb comes next, and the thing arriving comes last. The sentence draws attention to an arrival, a presence or a departure in what you can see or hear around you. The word here can get pointing stress, as if the speaker were pointing. When the arriving thing is a pronoun, the order is the ordinary one: Here it comes. A full noun phrase, like the bus, follows the verb. This dictionary treats the analysis as provisional.
curious.try: Say Here comes the bus, then Here it comes. Where does the thing arriving go in each?

teacher.summary: Helps explain Here comes the bus and Here it comes, where here or there with inversion draws attention to what is in view.
teacher.explain: The pattern has a stressed locative here or there, a verb and a full NP: Here comes the bus. It draws attention to an arrival, presence or departure in the perceptual setting. When the subject is a personal pronoun, the order is ordinary, with the pronoun before the verb: Here it comes. A full NP typically follows come. The locative can receive pointing stress, unlike the dummy subject of an existential. Compare presentational there, where there is a dummy subject. The analysis is provisional.
teacher.terms: Traditional grammars may describe here or there at the start as adverbs. This dictionary describes the locative as a deictic, pointing to the setting.
watch_for: A learner might treat here in Here comes the bus as a dummy subject like existential there, when it can take pointing stress.
A learner might think a pronoun should follow the verb in the same way a full noun phrase does.
teacher.activity: Students look out a window or at a picture and describe what is arriving or leaving with Here comes or There goes, using both a full noun phrase and a pronoun. They note where the stress falls.

child.hook: What do you say when you spot the bus coming?
child.explain: You can point at something with the word here at the start. Here comes the bus. When you use a word like it, it goes before the verb. Here it comes.
child.play: Stand at a window and watch. When something arrives, point and describe it with Here comes and the thing. Then say it again with just it.
